title: Fppf local models for pullbacks of an etale quotient map
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U,R$ be $S$-schemes, and let $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be a monomorphism identifying $R(W)$ with an equivalence relation on $U(W)$ for every $S$-scheme $W$. Suppose $s,t$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. On the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], let $F$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $W\mapsto U(W)/R(W)$, and let $q:h_U\to F$ be the canonical map, where $h_Z(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(W,Z)$. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume $s:R\to U$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. For every $S$-scheme $T$ and map $a:h_T\to F$, the presheaf $G$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}$ given by $G(W\xrightarrow{g}T)=\{u:W\to U\mid q(u)=a|_W\}$ is a sheaf of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. There exist an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ and maps $a_i:T_i\to U$ with $q(a_i)=a|_{T_i}$, together with natural identifications $G|_{T_i}\simeq h_{X_i}$, where $X_i=T_i\times_{a_i,U,s}R$. Under these identifications the map to $U$ is $t$ on the $R$-factor, and every $X_i\to T_i$ is separated and locally quasi-finite.

proof.text: For a covering $\{W_b\to W\}$ over $T$, the covering is fppf also as a family of $S$-schemes, hence fpqc by the existing Mathlib leaf [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc], applied to this same underlying family. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] with target $U$ to glue a matching family $u_b$ uniquely to $u:W\to U$. It is over $S$: its two composites to $S$ agree locally, hence agree by uniqueness in the same descent theorem with target $S$. Naturality gives $q(u)|_{W_b}=a|_{W_b}$, so the sheaf condition of $F$ gives $q(u)=a|_W$. This proves existence and uniqueness of gluing in $G$, including the empty covering.

source.place: Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms; Topologies Tag 022C; application to the subsheaf of lifts in Spaces Tag 0265.

proof.text: Put $P(W)=U(W)/R(W)$ and $\eta:P\to F$. The transformation $a:h_T\to F$ is determined by $a_T(\mathrm{id}_T)$: naturality gives $a_W(g)=F(g)(a_T(\mathrm{id}_T))$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] to this section, using the stated universe convention. Obtain an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ and classes $p_i\in P(T_i)$ mapping to $a|_{T_i}$. Choose representatives $a_i:T_i\to U$ of these quotient classes. Since $q(u)=\eta([u])$, they satisfy $q(a_i)=a|_{T_i}$.

source.place: Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification; Spaces Tag 0265, first representability step, local lifts.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-etale-relation-kernel-pair], $r\mapsto(sr,tr)$ gives a natural bijection $R(W)\simeq U(W)\times_{F(W)}U(W)$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given monomorphism and equivalence-relation hypotheses. For $g:W\to T_i$, substitute the pair $(a_i g,u)$. The equality $q(a_i g)=a|_W$ identifies $G(W)$ with $\{r:W\to R\mid sr=a_i g\}$. By [def-pc-fibre-product], this last set is $\operatorname{Mor}_{T_i}(W,T_i\times_{a_i,U,s}R)$. The maps in both directions send $u$ to the unique such $r$, and $r$ to $tr$. Uniqueness makes them inverse and compatible with every restriction $W'\to W$. Thus $G|_{T_i}\simeq h_{X_i}$ naturally, and its map to $U$ is $t$ on the $R$-factor.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, displayed fibre-product calculation, with s and t interchanged; kernel pair from Groupoids Tag 045Y.

proof.text: The projection $X_i=T_i\times_{a_i,U,s}R\to T_i$ is the base change of $s:R\to U$ along $a_i$. Apply the two clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change] to the assumed separatedness and local quasi-finiteness of $s$. Each projection is therefore separated and locally quasi-finite, as asserted.

lean.statement: theorem quotient_map_fppf_local_models {S : Scheme.{u}} {R U : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ U) [Mono (prod.lift s t)] (hrel : ∀ W : Over S, Equivalence (fun b c : W ⟶ U ↦ ∃ r : W ⟶ R, r ≫ s = b ∧ r ≫ t = c)) [Etale s.left] [Etale t.left] (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η : coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ⟶ F.obj) (hη : ∀ H : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun k : F.obj ⟶ H.obj ↦ η ≫ k)) [IsSeparated s.left] (hs : Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite s.left) (T : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ F.obj) : Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over T.left) (quotientMapFibre T F (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η) a) ∧ ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (Tᵢ : I → Over S) (f : ∀ i, Tᵢ i ⟶ T) (aᵢ : ∀ i, Tᵢ i ⟶ U), Presieve.ofArrows (fun i ↦ (Tᵢ i).left) (fun i ↦ (f i).left) ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T.left ∧ (∀ i, yoneda.map (aᵢ i) ≫ (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η) = yoneda.map (f i) ≫ a) ∧ (∀ i, ∃ e : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (pullback.fst (aᵢ i).left s.left)) ≅ (Over.map (f i).left).op ⋙ quotientMapFibre T F (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η) a, ∀ (W : Over (Tᵢ i).left) (x : W ⟶ Over.mk (pullback.fst (aᵢ i).left s.left)), (Subtype.val ((e.hom.app (op W)) x)).left = x.left ≫ pullback.snd (aᵢ i).left s.left ≫ t.left) ∧ (∀ i, IsSeparated (pullback.fst (aᵢ i).left s.left) ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite (pullback.fst (aᵢ i).left s.left))
